channel.description: Economy News: Get the Latest News on Indian Economy, Economic Indicators, Government Policy for Economy, Industries Fiscal & Monetary Measures. News & Analysis on Domestic and International Trade, National and State Finances, Budget, Government Regulation, Monetary Policy, RBI Rates, Interest Rates, CRR, Indian Trade, Monetary and Industrial Policy.

item.title: India-NZ FTA in force: Over half of New Zealand’s exports to India now tariff-free, Wellington also eyes Brazil, Canada
item.description: New Zealand is working to strengthen trade relations with Brazil and Canada in response to economic uncertainties. The country expects to complete the first New Zealand-Brazil Trade and Investment Dialogue after upcoming elections. A new free trade agreement with India has been implemented, making more than half of exports tariff-free. The agreement will benefit various products, including sheep meat and wool, as well as local businesses.

item.title: RBI injects Rs 1 lakh crore as liquidity tightens before festive season
item.description: On Monday, the RBI announced a Rs 1-lakh-crore variable rate repo (VRR) auction for the first time since late July after the weighted average call rate (WACR) at 5.67% on Monday, or 17 basis points higher than the repo rate of 5.50%. The central bank will conduct another VRR for Rs 50,000 crore on Wednesday.

item.title: China curbs spur push for local manufacturing
item.description: India's government will consult stakeholders on measures to mitigate the impact of Chinese export constraints. China recently imposed new restrictions on heavy machinery, such as tunnel boring machines, set to take effect soon. Indian officials assert that there should be no significant slowdown in highway development despite these curbs. The domestic construction industry is becoming increasingly self-sufficient regarding general equipment needs.

item.title: Finance Ministry to run financial inclusion campaign
item.description: The finance ministry is launching a campaign to saturate financial schemes across various local bodies. This initiative will reach 2.70 lakh gram panchayats and urban local bodies throughout India. Banks are expected to organize camps for enrolments and Aadhaar seeding for key schemes. The campaign will also involve updating nominations in savings accounts and providing other financial facilities.

item.title: RBI tightens scrutiny of $1 billion-plus overseas investments amid rupee pressure
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India is implementing stricter scrutiny on large overseas direct investments by Indian companies. Banks must now collect and present detailed information regarding these investments to the RBI. This initiative aims to prevent potential losses for both the companies and the Indian economy. The RBI's checklist requires banks to conduct thorough due diligence on the rationale behind each investment.

item.title: Uneven rains may keep price of spices elevated
item.description: Southern India is currently grappling with challenges in spice production, primarily due to uneven monsoon patterns and parched soil, which are adversely affecting harvest yields. Despite expanding cultivation areas, turmeric yields are predicted to plummet owing to unfavorable weather. Additionally, delays in red chilli sowing in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana could lead to surging market prices.

item.title: India-New Zealand FTA comes into effect today
item.description: The FTA will provide Indian exporters with 100% duty-free access to the New Zealand market, opening opportunities for MSMEs, women entrepreneurs, farmers and artisans. This is expected to facilitate $20 billion in investments into India in 15 years that would create opportunities across manufacturing, infrastructure, agriculture, and innovation.

item.title: Tariff quota notified for New Zealand fruits, honey
item.description: Kiwifruit imports will qualify for zero customs duty under the tariff rate quota (TRQ), subject to a minimum CIF value of $1.80 per kg while 40 tonnes of New Zealand-certified Manuka honey under the quota have been permitted for 2026. The annual limit will increase to 200 tonnes from 2027.

item.title: CBDT exempts interest payments on rupee-denominated bonds issued by New Development Bank from TDS
item.description: The exemption applies to holders of Maharajah INR Bonds who are Indian residents or foreign institutional investors, for the 2026-27 tax year and subsequent tax years.

item.title: India-New Zealand FTA kicks in October 20, gives all Indian goods zero-duty access
item.description: India's free trade agreement with New Zealand will begin on October 20 and provide duty-free access for Indian goods. This agreement aims to boost bilateral trade significantly by 2030, increasing it from $2.4 billion to nearly ₹35,000 crore. New Zealand will grant 100% market access, while India will provide tariff concessions on 70% of its tariff lines. Customs clearance timelines will be expedited, enhancing trade efficiency and reducing costs.

item.title: India sets import quotas for New Zealand apples, kiwifruit under FTA
item.description: India will implement a quota system for importing apples, kiwifruit, Manuka honey, and albumins from New Zealand. The quotas will gradually increase over five years, allowing for proper regulation of imports. Apple imports will be capped initially, with no allowances in the first year. The duty rates will vary depending on the product and its CIF value, affecting import dynamics.

item.title: India-New Zealand FTA to kick in October 20, opening market opportunities for exporters
item.description: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement will come into effect on October 20, enhancing trade for both nations. New Zealand expects increased demand for its agricultural products, particularly kiwifruit, honey, and apples, in India. The agreement includes provisions to ensure tariff-free access for Indian goods in New Zealand's market. Both countries aim to strengthen economic ties and improve productivity in agricultural sectors.

item.title: India probing Pernod, Diageo Scotch imports under India-UK trade pact, sources say
item.description: Indian tax officials are investigating Pernod Ricard and Diageo for how they classified bulk Scotch imports. These companies may have improperly benefitted from reduced tariffs under a recent trade agreement. Tax inspectors made surprising visits to both companies' offices to gather information about their practices. The investigations are part of a broader scrutiny faced by foreign investors in India.

item.title: China announces export curbs on key machinery used in India's infrastructure development
item.description: Beijing has announced new export controls on essential machinery, which will impact India's infrastructure development. These restrictions will take effect on November 18 and apply to tunnel boring machines and related items. Additionally, the export controls include walking excavators and specific dredger-related items, complicating several Indian projects.

item.title: NABVENTURES plans Rs 30-70 crore bets on growth-stage firms in Fund II
item.description: NABVENTURES aims to invest ₹30-70 crore per company in agriculture, rural financial services, and climate solutions. The venture capital arm plans to focus on technology-driven businesses and growth-stage companies with established traction. Larger initial checks will be adapted for follow-on funding in high-performing portfolio companies. The emphasis will be on sustainable scaling in large markets, improving productivity, and raising farmers' incomes.

item.title: Trump waives Russia sanctions, easing India’s energy concerns as US trade deal nears
item.description: US President Donald Trump waived key Russian sanctions which may enhance trade relations with India. This decision is expected to provide negotiating space for a potential trade deal. India, one of the largest importers of Russian oil, faces challenges due to declining imports. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is visiting India to discuss cooperation on this matter. The waiver could help India secure more favorable tariffs while stabilizing energy policies.

item.title: Textiles Ministry identifies 4,000 startups for export growth support
item.description: The textiles ministry has identified over 4,000 textile-based startups for support to scale up and become export-ready over the next three to four years. Consultations with registered startups and small businesses are expected to begin in late November or early December, followed by a national startup conclave in December to assess their needs.

item.title: RDI fund to spur 10-fold investment from private sector, says NITI's Abhay Karandikar
item.description: The Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) scheme aims to significantly increase private sector investment in India. It is designed to catalyse nearly Rs 10-lakh crore in investment over the next ten years while creating new job opportunities. The focus will be on crucial technology areas like artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and space technologies.

item.title: America very close to finalising trade deal with India: Marco Rubio
US very close to finalising trade deal with India, says Marco Rubio
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that Washington is close to finalising a trade deal with India. He said the US considers various factors, including ongoing trade negotiations, while making decisions on national security waivers related to Russian oil and gas sanctions.

item.title: Exporters may be asked to monitor supply chains' indirect emissions
item.description: The Indian government is engaging in discussions about measuring Scope 3 emissions for exporters. This consideration arises as trade partners impose tighter green requirements globally. Current frameworks focus on direct emissions and exclude indirect ones, making compliance more complex. As a result, industries, especially MSMEs, may face compliance burdens if new requirements are implemented. Ultimately, the aim is to ensure that Indian exporters remain competitive in international markets.

item.title: Farmers face 15% loss as poultry feed costs surge
item.description: Poultry farmers are currently experiencing losses of approximately 15% due to rising livestock feed costs. Key ingredients have seen price increases of up to 75%, affecting farmers' ability to cope. Dairy producers, particularly in drought-affected regions, struggle to source necessary fodder for their livestock. Feed manufacturers are also feeling the impact as higher prices reduce demand for their products.

item.title: Global investors against use of judicial anti-avoidance rule by tax officials
item.description: International investors have raised concerns regarding the Indian Income-tax authorities' invocation of the judicial anti-avoidance rule. At a recent meeting, investors communicated their issues with the Central Board of Direct Taxes on this matter. The use of JAAR to deny relief on grandfathered shares contradicts prior regulations established by the CBDT. The standing of both GAAR and JAAR remains complex due to Supreme Court rulings.

item.title: India's exports rise across geographies; Africa, ASEAN lead growth in Apr-Aug
item.description: India's merchandise exports increased significantly across different regions from April to August this fiscal year. Exports to Africa saw a notable rise of 47 percent, reaching USD 26.19 billion. The ASEAN region also experienced a substantial growth of 56 percent in exports, totaling USD 23.08 billion. Furthermore, shipments to North-East Asia rose by 37 percent, amounting to USD 21.03 billion. Overall, India's total merchandise exports rose by 18.

item.title: Faster services imports threaten to erode cushion against India’s goods trade deficit: Report
item.description: India's services trade surplus has declined as imports grew faster than exports, leading to concerns about foreign exchange earnings. In September 2026, net services exports fell by 10 percent to USD 16.9 billion. Despite strong growth in merchandise exports of 23 percent, the services sector faces challenges. While cumulative net services exports increased during the first half, their sustainability is uncertain.

item.title: India needs policy credibility and continuity to sustain FDI as strong growth alone is not enough, says KIEP expert
item.description: India needs to maintain policy credibility and continuity to sustain foreign investment inflows, as strong economic growth alone may not be enough to reassure global investors about the country's long-term business environment, highlighted Kyunghoon Kim, Head of the India and South Asia Team at the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy (KIEP).

item.title: What is holding up the US-India trade deal?
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will visit India next week to strengthen bilateral relations and discuss trade issues. His meetings will take place in Mumbai and Jamnagar, focusing on investment and energy. The two countries have faced considerable delays in finalizing a trade agreement due to several ongoing challenges.

item.title: 'India an important ally': Rubio says Trump studying effects of tariffs on countries like India
India’s soybean output seen falling 2.1% to 107.93 lakh tonnes in Kharif 2026: Farmers' body
item.description: India's soybean production forecast indicates a slight decline to 107.93 lakh tonnes during the ongoing Kharif season. Drought-like conditions in Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana are contributing to this reduction in output. However, increased production in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan is expected to compensate for these losses. The area cultivated with soybean increased by approximately 5 lakh hectares compared to the previous season.

item.title: 'India an important ally': Rubio says Trump weighing impact of Russia-related tariffs
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that India's energy requirements will be considered before possible sanctions on Russian oil. President Donald Trump recently waived certain provisions of a proposed sanctions law affecting major importers of Russian crude. Rubio emphasized the need for time to assess the impact of these measures on global economies. He highlighted the strategic partnership with India as an important factor in decision-making.

item.title: Christmas cheer, but caution remains: Exporters welcome US tariff relief, keep diversification plans
item.description: US President Donald Trump’s decision to waive proposed tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian oil has eased uncertainty for Indian exporters ahead of the crucial Christmas shipping season. However, businesses across textiles, gems and jewellery, and human hair products say they will continue diversifying export markets after last year’s tariff turmoil, even as the US remains a key destination for Indian goods.

item.title: India notifies first tariff cuts under New Zealand FTA
item.description: India will implement duty concessions for certain imports from New Zealand starting October 20, under a new FTA. The concessions include zero basic customs duty for sheep meat and specific rates for fish and wine. Additionally, provisions have been made for manuka honey and kiwi fruit imports with varying duties. Sensitive categories like dairy products are excluded from this trade liberalization agreement.

item.title: Commerce Ministry organizes “Leveraging FTAs” outreach program in Jaipur to boost exports
item.description: The Commerce Ministry organized an outreach event in Jaipur, targeting exporters to clarify the use of benefits provided by India's free trade agreements. This initiative aims to translate preferential market access into tangible export opportunities for Indian enterprises, emphasizing Rajasthan's strengths in textiles, handicrafts, and gems. Plans for coordination among stakeholders are outlined to optimize support for exporters moving forward.

item.title: Rs 3,600 crore business enquiries at 5-day handicraft fair
item.description: Over 7,300 buyers participated in the 62nd IHGF Delhi Fair held from October 13 to 17. Business enquiries at the fair totaled Rs 3,600 crore, demonstrating strong international interest. Buyers from 105 countries, including the US, UK, and Germany, were present. Many brands indicated a significant shift toward sourcing more products from Indian manufacturers. India's handicraft exports reached $3.75 billion for the fiscal year 2025-26.

item.title: US' Russia sanction waiver a relief for India's exporters, energy security: Experts
item.description: The waiver of sanctions under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act provides relief for India's energy security. Experts believe that continued access to Russian crude will support economic growth and ease inflationary pressures. While the waiver offers temporary relief, uncertainty remains regarding future contracts and investments. Trade organizations express hope for improving bilateral trade relations and advancing discussions between India and the US.

item.title: Who will pay for today's optimism if AI goes wrong? CEA Anantha Nageswaran answers
item.description: Chief Economic Adviser Anantha Nageswaran raised concerns over the financial risks linked to artificial intelligence. He stated that finance ministries, central banks, and households could face costs from misplaced optimism. Even if AI expectations are met, these entities may still incur expenses. Nageswaran intends to outline five specific risks regarding this issue. He plans to suggest potential government actions to mitigate these risks in future discussions.

item.title: Trump’s 100% Russian oil tariff U-turn has a catch India can’t ignore
item.description: GTRI has warned that Donald Trump’s waiver of threatened 100% tariffs on Russian oil buyers offers India only temporary relief, as Washington can reinstate the duties at any time. The think tank cited US purchases of Russian diesel, tariff protection for China and ongoing India-US trade talks as possible reasons for the move. It also urged New Delhi to protect its energy security and avoid permanent trade concessions in exchange for reversible tariff relief.

item.title: India notifies first New Zealand FTA duty cuts; sheep meat gets zero duty, kiwi fruit at 15%
item.description: India has notified the first set of customs duty concessions for imports from New Zealand under their free trade agreement, effective October 20. The preferential rates cover products such as wine, manuka honey, kiwi fruit and sheep meat, with limited quantities of select goods allowed under tariff-rate quotas and dairy and other sensitive sectors excluded.

item.title: ‘For global trade’s sake, hope our US deal is inked soon’: FM Nirmala Sitharaman
item.description: Nirmala Sitharaman expressed optimism regarding the speedy conclusion of the India-US trade agreement during her recent interaction. She highlighted challenges in trade relations with China due to non-tariff barriers causing problems for Indian exporters. The Finance Minister advocated for promoting rupee-denominated trade settlements to assist nations experiencing hard currency shortages. Sitharaman emphasized the importance of public investment in infrastructure to bolster economic growth despite global disruptions.

item.title: No meddling as 'middlemen' in forex conversion by banks: New rules forbid conversion of foreign earnings into rupees to detriment of exporters
item.description: The Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India (FEDAI) has directed banks not to convert foreign currency remittances into rupees without specific instructions from the sender or beneficiary. The move follows concerns that intermediary banks were converting dollars at unfavourable exchange rates, leaving small exporters and individuals receiving overseas payments with less money. Banks have also been asked to ensure transparent forex service charges and disclose currency conversion rates on their websites.

item.title: Government approves Rs 1,195 crore for ITI cluster modernisation
item.description: With these approvals, the cumulative investment approved under the scheme has reached ₹3,687 crore to date to help transform ITIs into modern, industry-aligned and future-ready skill institutions.

item.title: India should become a tech-creator rather than tech-user nation: Niti Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Lahiri
item.description: Niti Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Lahiri stressed the need for rapid economic reforms and structural changes to help India become a developed nation by 2047. "Technological progress is needed to compete with the rest of the world," he said.

item.title: 'India needs 8-9% growth to become a developed nation by 2047'
item.description: India aims to become a $30 trillion economy by 2047, from its current size of around $4 trillion. The country's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 7.8% in the June quarter, exceeding expectations.

item.title: White House lists investment over $330 billion in US from India
item.description: The White House announced investments of over $330 billion from India as part of total investments. This total is reported as $10.871 trillion from various countries and private industries. Specific investments included $310 billion and $20.5 billion, plus a $15 billion steel plant by Essar Group. US President Donald Trump previously mentioned Reliance Industries' $300 billion investment in Texas.

item.title: Nirmala Sitharaman pitches for public, private capital to build financially sustainable cities
item.description: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman highlighted the importance of creating sustainably investable cities in India. She proposed a combination of public investment alongside private capital to achieve these goals. Various urban development initiatives have been established to support this approach effectively. The Urban Challenge Fund aims to improve municipal finances and is pivotal for project preparation. Overall, the strategies discussed will enhance urban planning and infrastructure development throughout the country.

item.title: China says ready to address each other's concerns after Sitharaman flags trade barriers
item.description: China said it was ready to work with India to allay its concerns of rising trade imbalance. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said the trade imbalance was due to China's restrictions in market access to Indian goods and services. She said that India has not resorted to punitive tariffs to reign in large trade imbalances and prefers negotiations despite the process being time-consuming.

item.title: National highway projects awarded rise 62.9% during April-Sept: MoSPI
item.description: National highway projects awarded experienced a 62.9% increase in distance during the April-September period. Electronic toll collection transactions also rose significantly, indicating increased digital use. Air cargo movement increased by 12%, and foreign tourist arrivals grew as well. The telecommunications sector expanded, adding over 29,000 kilometers of optical fiber cable. Overall, performance indicators across multiple infrastructure sectors have shown positive trends in FY27.

item.title: India's forex reserves shed $60 billion in six weeks as RBI steps in to support rupee, one of Asia's worst-performing currencies this year
item.description: India’s foreign exchange reserves declined by nearly $60 billion in six weeks to $726.027 billion as of October 9, from a record high of $785.706 billion on September 4. The fall was largely attributed to the Reserve Bank of India’s intervention to support the rupee amid rising crude oil prices, higher US yields and sustained foreign investor outflows. Foreign currency assets and gold reserves also recorded significant declines during the reporting week.

item.title: India needs to leverage FTAs, export promotion mission initiatives to boost shipments: CII's Budhia
item.description: Indian businesses are encouraged to utilise free trade agreements and the export promotion mission for expansion. Recent data shows that India’s merchandise exports have increased significantly over the past year. Services exports show a small decline yet cumulative growth remains positive compared to last year. Ongoing efforts aim to strengthen India’s overall export capabilities and international partnerships.

item.title: India to reach 100 billion dollar of bilateral trade with Russia by 2030: Ambassador Vinay Kumar
item.description: India is pursuing negotiations for a Free Trade Agreement with the Eurasian Economic Union to increase exports. Indian Ambassador to Russia Vinay Kumar stated that bilateral trade is projected to reach USD 100 billion by 2030. The current trade turnover is reported at USD 38 billion for the first half of this year. Efforts are underway to diversify India's export basket and improve market access in Russia.
